newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Eurotel to launch second Slovak GSM system in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Eurotel to launch second Slovak GSM system in Feb.

text.p: The U.S.-Slovak mobile telephone joint-venture Eurotel Bratislava on Friday said it would launch operation of the second Slovak digital GSM system by the end of February 1997.
Eurotel's Director Artur Bobovnicky told Reuters that the the company would invest roughly six billion crowns into building the network.
"Today we started the test operation and the commercial operation will be launched by the end of February," Bobovnicky said.
He declined to elaborate on the sources and schedule for the investment plans.
Eurotel is owned by the Slovak state-run fixed line monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie s.p., and U.S. groups Bell Atlantic Corp and U.S. West Media Group Inc.

Since 1991 the three companies operated the sole Slovak mobile telephone network, an analogue NMT system, through Eurotel s.r.o., in which ST held 51 percent and the two U.S. telecom groups together had 49 percent.
Last September, the Slovak ministry of telecomunications formally granted the second Slovak GSM licence to Eurotel s.r.o. under the contract for the NMT system.
But the licence was issued with the clause that Eurotel's owners must conform to the government's 60 percent Slovak ownership condition.
The three owners on December 16 agreed to reduce stake of the U.S. firms to 40 percent and to transform Eurotel to a joint-stock company from its previous statute of a public limited company,
The overall GSM penetration in Slovakia is expected to be some 11 percent by the year 2006.
Eurotel said its market share should be around 50 percent by that time.
Eurotel's only competitor in Slovakia will Globtel a.s., which said earlier this week that it would start operating its GSM system on January 15.

Globtel is a consortium of four Slovak state-owned energy companies, the state- owned monopoly gas distributor SPP and the private firm Hanco sro, which teamed up with France Telecom Mobile International (FTMI) to win a government tender for one of the two Slovak GSM licences earlier this year.
